issues.legal_issue: A taxpayer’s agreement to apply part of rental income to another person after the right to the full rent has accrued does not divert that income from the taxpayer.
material_facts: The family owned property leased to a company for annual rent.
The lease made the full rent payable to the family, with part of it to be paid directly to a college.
A later agreement gave the college a right to recover that part from the company and a charge securing payment.
The obligation to pay the college arose from the family’s agreement, not from an antecedent independent title held by the college.
issues.conclusion: The entire rental income was taxable to the family; the payment to the college was an application of income, not a diversion of it.
issues.legal_principle: Under the distinction stated in C.I.T. v. Sitaldas Tirathdas, income is diverted where an antecedent and independent obligation prevents it from becoming the taxpayer’s income; a self-imposed or gratuitous obligation to pay another after income accrues is merely an application of income. The Court relied on C.I.T. v. Sitaldas Tirathdas, Murlidhar Himmatsingka v. I.T.O., and Mahaliram Santhalia v. C.I.T. It also noted that section 24(1)(iv) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, as amended, treated voluntarily created annual charges differently, although that provision did not govern this case.

rule.if: rental_income_tax_assessment and taxpayer_owns_leased_property and full_rent_accrues_to_taxpayer and payment_obligation_is_self_imposed

predicates.rental_income_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns whether rental income is taxable in an income-tax assessment.
predicates.taxpayer_owns_leased_property: The taxpayer owns the property that is leased to a tenant.
predicates.full_rent_accrues_to_taxpayer: The lease makes the full rent payable to the taxpayer, even if some is paid directly to another person.
predicates.payment_obligation_is_self_imposed: The taxpayer’s obligation to pay part of the rent to another person arises from the taxpayer’s own agreement and not from that person’s antecedent independent title.

issues.definition: When rental income is assessed, if the taxpayer owns the leased property, the full rent accrues to the taxpayer, and the obligation to pay another person is self-imposed, the entire rental income is taxable to the taxpayer.

issues.legal_issue: A settlor who is also the sole trustee can create a valid trust over immovable property by declaration, without conveying the property to trustees, if the declaration and conduct show an intention to surrender beneficial ownership and hold the property exclusively as trustee.
material_facts: The family’s karta executed a trust deed declaring that income from specified properties would belong to the trust and would not be used for his personal benefit.
The karta constituted himself the sole trustee under the original deed.
The trust deed specified charitable and religious purposes for the income and restricted the owner’s use of the properties.
The family’s subsequent conduct and a later deed supported the trust arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The trust was valid, the income was diverted at source, and the income from the properties was not assessable to the family under the applicable exemption provisions.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the Indian Trusts Act permits a settlor who is himself the trustee to vest trust property through a declaration showing a clear intention to divest himself of beneficial interest and to exercise control exclusively as trustee; a registered conveyance to trustees is necessary when the trustees are persons other than the author, but not when the author is the sole trustee. Income from property held under a trust or other legal obligation for qualifying purposes is exempt under section 4(3)(i) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, and section 11(1)(a) of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

rule.if: charitable_trust_income_assessment and settlor_is_sole_trustee and declaration_shows_divestment_of_beneficial_interest and property_held_exclusively_as_trustee and income_applied_exclusively_to_charitable_purposes

predicates.charitable_trust_income_assessment: The proceeding concerns whether income from property placed in a charitable trust is assessable to the settlor.
predicates.settlor_is_sole_trustee: The person who declares the trust is also its sole trustee.
predicates.declaration_shows_divestment_of_benefici: The declaration, read with the settlor’s conduct, clearly shows an intention to give up personal beneficial interest in the property.
predicates.property_held_exclusively_as_trustee: The settlor exercises dominion and control over the property only in the capacity of trustee.
predicates.income_applied_exclusively_to_charitable: The income from the property is required to be used exclusively for charitable purposes.

issues.definition: When charitable-trust income is assessed, if the settlor is the sole trustee, the declaration shows divestment of beneficial interest, the property is held exclusively as trustee, and its income is applied exclusively to charitable purposes, the trust income is not assessable to the settlor.
